originalTitle: Sudan's invisible children - born in war with no legal identity
title: Every Child Needs a Name: Helping Kids in Sudan
content:
Hello, Super Friends!

Hello there, super friends from all over! Your friend from Africa is here today to share a very important story. It's about a country called Sudan, which is far away on our amazing continent of Africa. Sometimes, sad and difficult things happen in Sudan, just like in other parts of the world. There is a war happening in Sudan. A war is when people fight, and it makes it very unsafe for everyone. It's especially hard for children and their mummies and daddies. Imagine having to leave your home because it's not safe. That's what many families in Sudan have to do.

What is a Birth Certificate?

Do you have a birthday? Of course you do! And you have a name, right? Well, a birth certificate is a very special piece of paper. It’s like your official 'hello' to the whole world! This important paper has your name, your birthday, and where you were born. It proves that you are a real person and that you are here! It’s like a special ID card for babies and children. Did you know? In most places around the world, getting a birth certificate is one of the very first things parents do when their new baby arrives! It’s a very happy and important moment.

Why is a Birth Certificate Important?

Let's imagine why this paper is so, so important. Think about it: when you want to go to school, you usually need to show your birth certificate. It helps the school know your age and that you are ready to learn and play with new friends. If you get sick and need to see a doctor, sometimes they ask for it too. It helps them know who you are and how best to help you. Later, when you grow up, you might need it for a job or to travel and explore new places. Most importantly, it means you are counted! Your country knows you are part of their big family. It means you are not 'invisible' to the world. Every child has rights, and having a birth certificate helps make sure your rights are protected. Did you know? The United Nations, which is like a big team of countries working together, says that every child has a right to a name and a nationality! This means every child should belong to a country and be counted.

Children in Sudan Need Our Help

Now, let's go back to Sudan. Because of the war, many mummies there are in very, very difficult situations. Imagine giving birth to a baby when you are hiding, or when you are far away from your home and any safe hospitals. It becomes very, very hard for these mummies to go to a special office to get that important birth certificate for their babies. Sometimes, there are no offices open because of the fighting, or it's too dangerous to even travel. So, many new babies born in Sudan don't get this special paper. They are like 'invisible children' because their country doesn't officially know they are there. This is very sad, because every child deserves to be seen. Did you know? When there is a war, everything becomes much, much harder for families, especially for little babies and children who need lots of care and safety.

What Happens Without a Birth Certificate?

Think about what happens if you don't have this important paper. It's very hard to go to school. No school means no learning to read or write, no fun with friends, and no chance to learn amazing new things. It's also hard to see a doctor if you get sick. This means babies and children might not get the medicine or help they need to feel better and grow strong. They might not get special vaccines to keep them healthy. Later, when they grow up, it's hard to get a job or even to travel safely to find a new, safe home. These children might feel like they don't belong, or that nobody sees them, even if their mummy loves them very much. Did you know? All around the world, kind people and big helper organizations like UNICEF are working very hard to make sure every child can get their birth certificate and be counted.

What Can We Do?

So, what can we do to help these invisible children in Sudan? Well, lots of grown-ups and special helper organizations are working very, very hard right now. They are trying to create safe places where mummies can go to get birth certificates for their babies, even during difficult times. They are also talking to important leaders and telling everyone that every single child in Sudan needs to be seen and counted. They are saying that every child deserves a birth certificate, no matter what. We can also help by learning and talking about it! Even kids like us can share this story with our families and friends. When we share, more people learn, and more people want to help. This creates a big wave of kindness. Did you know? When you learn about problems in the world, you become a kind of superhero! By caring and sharing, you help spread awareness and hope.

Every Child Matters!

Every single child, no matter where they are born or how difficult their start, deserves to be counted. Every child deserves a name, a birthday, and a piece of paper that says, 'Hello, world! I am here!' Having a birth certificate helps children go to school, see doctors, and grow up strong and happy. It helps them have a bright future. We hope that soon, all the invisible children in Sudan will become visible to everyone. We hope they get their birth certificates and all the chances they deserve to live happy, healthy lives. Let's remember to be kind and think about all the children in the world. You are important, and so are all the children in Sudan!
summary: Many children born in Sudan during the war don't have a special paper called a birth certificate, which means they are not officially counted and miss out on important things like school and doctors.
whyMatters: This is important because every child needs a birth certificate to prove who they are, go to school, see a doctor, and have a good future, and children without one can feel like they don't belong.

originalTitle: Does Africa still back Infantino as Fifa president?
title: Who Will Lead Africa's Big Football Family?
content:
Hello, Football Friends!

Hello, amazing young football fans across Africa! It's your friendly news reporter here, ready to talk about something super important: our favourite game, football! We all love to watch our teams play, don't we? The cheers, the goals, the excitement – it’s the best! Today, we're talking about the big boss of world football and what our African football family thinks. Did you know? Football is the most popular sport in Africa! Almost everyone loves to kick a ball around, from the smallest villages to the biggest cities.

What is FIFA?

Imagine a very, very big club for all the football teams in the whole world. That big club is called FIFA! FIFA helps to make sure football is played fair, and that everyone can enjoy it. They help organize giant tournaments, like the World Cup, where teams from different countries play against each other to see who is the best. Did you know? FIFA stands for the 'International Federation of Association Football'. It was started way back in 1904!

Who is Mr. Infantino?

Every big club needs a leader, right? Just like your school has a head teacher, or your football team has a captain. The leader of FIFA is called the President. His name is Mr. Gianni Infantino. He is like the main person who helps make big decisions for football all over the world. He travels a lot, meets people from different countries, and tries to make football better for everyone. He helps decide where the next big tournaments will be and how to help countries play more football.

Why is Africa Important to Football?

Africa is a huge, wonderful continent with so much talent! We have some of the best football players in the world. Many African teams also play wonderfully in big competitions. Our continent has a big voice in world football because so many people here love and play the game. When the FIFA President makes big decisions, he really needs to listen to what Africa thinks. Did you know? African players like Mohamed Salah, Sadio Mané, and Victor Osimhen are famous all over the world for their incredible football skills!

What Does "Backing" Mean?

Our big question today is: Does Africa still "back" Mr. Infantino? What does "back" mean? It means, do the football leaders in Africa still think he is doing a good job? Do they still support him as the leader of world football? It's like asking if your friends still think your team captain is the best person to lead the team. Sometimes, leaders are chosen for a few years. When that time is almost up, people think about who should be the leader next. African football leaders are thinking about this now. They want what is best for football in Africa and for the whole world.

How FIFA Helps African Football

FIFA helps African football in many ways. They give money to build new football fields so more children can play. They help train coaches to teach kids how to play better. They also help to organize local football games and tournaments. This means more children can dream of becoming great football stars one day! Mr. Infantino has visited many countries in Africa. He has promised to help African football grow even bigger and better. He wants more African teams to play in the World Cup. He wants more money to come to Africa to help build stadiums and develop young players. Did you know? The World Cup is held every four years, and it's the biggest football party on Earth!

The African Football Family (CAF)

Just like FIFA is a big club for the world, Africa has its own big football family! It's called CAF. CAF stands for the 'Confederation of African Football'. All the football countries in Africa are part of CAF. CAF helps organize big African tournaments, like the Africa Cup of Nations, where African countries play each other. CAF is like the voice of African football. When they make a decision, it means all the countries in Africa are speaking together. They haven't officially said yet if they fully support Mr. Infantino for his next time as president. They are talking and thinking about it very carefully.

What Do Our Countries Think?

Many African countries have very strong football teams. Their leaders in football are thinking about what is best for the future. Let's look at some important countries and what their football bosses might be thinking.

Nigeria's Roar!

Nigeria has a super strong team called the Super Eagles! They have lots of amazing players. Nigeria's football leaders want to make sure that decisions made by FIFA help their young players grow and give them more chances to play on the world stage. They want fair play and good support for African teams.

Egypt's Magic!

Egypt is famous for its fantastic football, especially players like Mohamed Salah. The football leaders in Egypt want to see more investments in African football. They want more resources for training and better football facilities. They hope for a leader who truly cares about African talent.

Senegal's Lions!

Senegal's national team, the Teranga Lions, are very strong! They have won the Africa Cup of Nations. Senegal's football leaders want to make sure Africa has a strong voice in FIFA. They want a leader who listens to African needs and helps to develop football from the smallest local teams all the way up to the national team.

South Africa's Bafana Bafana!

South Africa, also known as the Bafana Bafana, once hosted the FIFA World Cup! That was a very special time. South Africa's football leaders understand how important good leadership is. They want a FIFA president who will help all countries, big or small, to have fair opportunities in football. Did you know? The 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa was the first time the tournament was held on the African continent!

Morocco's Atlas Lions!

Morocco's Atlas Lions had an amazing journey in the last World Cup, reaching the semi-finals! They showed the whole world how strong African football can be. Morocco's football leaders are very proud and want to make sure FIFA continues to support and celebrate African success on the global stage. They look for a leader who values all football-playing nations.

Ghana's Black Stars!

Ghana's Black Stars are another powerful team from Africa. They have been to the World Cup many times! Ghana's football leaders want a FIFA president who will keep helping African teams grow and compete at the highest level. They believe in teamwork and fair chances for everyone in the football world.

Keeping Football Fun!

So, all these important people from our African football family are thinking carefully. They want to choose the best leader for FIFA. They want someone who will make sure football stays fun, fair, and exciting for all of us, especially for all the young boys and girls who dream of playing football one day. We will have to wait and see what they decide! No matter what, one thing is for sure: Africa will always love football! And our amazing players will keep shining brightly on pitches around the world. Did you know? The word 'football' is called 'soccer' in some countries, like South Africa and the USA, but it's the same beautiful game!
summary: African football leaders are thinking about whether to continue supporting Mr. Gianni Infantino as the big boss of FIFA, the global football organization, because they want what is best for football across Africa.
whyMatters: This is important because the leader of FIFA helps make big decisions about football all over the world, including in Africa, and African leaders want to make sure our continent's football grows bigger and better for all kids to enjoy.

originalTitle: DR Congo river boat under quarantine for Ebola after five deaths
title: Keeping Everyone Safe on the Big River!
content:
A Trip on the Big River

Imagine a big, long river that is like a watery road! In a country called DR Congo, many friendly people travel on these boats. It's how they visit family or go to market to buy and sell things. One day, a big boat was traveling on a very important river. This river is called the Congo River. It is one of the biggest and longest rivers in all of Africa! Many boats use it every single day.

Doctors Are Helping Friends

On this boat, some people started to feel very, very sick. It was a special kind of sickness called Ebola. It's a bit like a very bad flu, but it needs extra special care from doctors. When the doctors found out, they quickly came to help. They are like real-life superheroes! Their most important job is to keep everyone healthy and safe, just like your parents keep you safe.

What is Ebola?

Ebola is a sickness caused by tiny, tiny germs. These germs are so small, you cannot even see them with your eyes! But they can make people feel very unwell and tired. Did you know? Germs are everywhere around us, but most of them are not bad. Some germs can make us sick, and that's why we always wash our hands with soap and water! Doctors and nurses know a lot about Ebola. They have special medicines and ways to help people get better and strong again. They work very, very hard to fight these tricky germs.

A Special Safety Check

To keep everyone safe, the doctors decided to do a special safety check. They asked all the people on the boat to stay in one safe place for a little while. This special timeout is called "quarantine." Quarantine is like a special, gentle timeout for a group. It helps make sure that if anyone has those tiny germs, they don't accidentally share them with others. It's a very smart way to stop the sickness from spreading to more people. All the passengers on the boat are being looked after very carefully. Doctors are checking everyone to make sure they are okay and not feeling sick. This checking is called "screening." Did you know? Screening means doctors ask questions about how you feel and look. They might take your temperature too, just like your mommy or daddy does when you have a fever to see if you are hot.

Hero Doctors and Nurses

Our doctors and nurses are very brave and kind. They wear special clothes to protect themselves from the tiny germs. These clothes look like astronaut suits or big raincoats! They check on everyone on the boat every single day. They give them yummy food and clean water to drink. They also give special medicine to those who need it to help them feel better. These wonderful people are working day and night without stopping. They want to make sure everyone on the boat stays healthy and happy. They are making sure the tiny germs go away for good.

Keeping Our Communities Safe

This special safety check is very important for everyone in the DR Congo. It helps protect not just the people on the boat, but also their families, friends, and whole communities. Did you know? DR Congo is a very, very big country in Africa. It has beautiful green forests, mighty rivers, and many friendly people who live there! By being careful now, we can stop the sickness from bothering more people. It's like putting up a strong fence to keep something bad from getting out and hurting others. It helps everyone stay well.

What Can Kids Do?

Even though you are little, you can help too! The very best thing you can do is wash your hands often and very well. Use soap and water, and sing "Happy Birthday" twice while you scrub your hands! Washing your hands helps chase away all those tiny, invisible germs. It's like giving your hands a super shower! Clean hands mean fewer germs and less sickness for everyone. Also, always listen to your parents and teachers. They always want to keep you safe and healthy. If you ever feel sick or unwell, tell a grown-up right away so they can help you.

Everyone Is Working Together

So, remember, everyone is working together like a big team. The doctors, the nurses, and even the people on the boat are helping. They all want to make sure everyone is safe and healthy and feeling good. Soon, everyone on the boat will be able to go home to their families. They will be happy and healthy again, thanks to all the brave helpers! It shows how much we care for each other in Africa. Did you know? When people work together, like doctors and nurses and you, they can solve big problems and help many, many people!
summary: Doctors in DR Congo are helping people on a river boat stay safe and healthy after some felt sick, by checking everyone and making sure germs don't spread to protect the community.
whyMatters: This matters because doctors are working very hard to stop a sickness called Ebola from spreading, which helps keep many people and their families safe and healthy in DR Congo.

originalTitle: Trump denies US weapons shortage and says information 'leakers' being 'hunted down'
title: Secrets, Special Tools, and Speaking the Truth!
content:
Hello from Your News Friend!

Jambo, my wonderful friends! It's your friendly news reporter for Africa here, ready to share some interesting news with you. We're going to talk about something that might sound a little bit grown-up, but I promise we'll make it super easy to understand. Think of it like a story! We want to learn about the world, right?

What Are We Talking About Today?

Today, we're talking about a very important person named Mr. Trump. He used to be the leader of a big country far away called America, or the United States. He said something about special tools that armies use and about people who tell secrets. Don't worry, we'll break it down piece by piece, just like eating a delicious fruit!

Who is Mr. Trump?

Imagine your school principal, but for a whole country! Mr. Trump was like that for the United States. He was the president, which means he was in charge and made many big decisions for his country and its people. Sometimes, leaders have to talk about important things, even things that are a bit serious. Did you know? The United States is a very big country, much bigger than many countries in Africa! It has many, many people living there.

What Are "Tools for Armies"?

Sometimes, countries have armies to keep their people safe. Armies use special tools to help them do their job. When we talk about "weapons," we just mean these special tools. They are not like your toy cars or building blocks. These tools are made for grown-ups in the army, to protect their country. Mr. Trump was talking about these special tools. He said that his country, the United States, has enough of these tools. He said they are not running out. It's like if someone asked you, "Do you have enough pencils for school?" and you say, "Yes, I have plenty!"

When We Talk About "Shortage"

What does "shortage" mean? Imagine you have a box of your favourite crayons. If you use too many of one colour, like red, and you suddenly don't have any red crayons left, that's a shortage! It means you don't have enough of something. So, some people thought America might have a shortage of their special army tools, but Mr. Trump said, "No, we don't! We have enough!" Did you know? Sometimes, if there is a shortage of something important, like water, people have to be very careful not to waste it!

Secrets, Secrets, Everywhere!

Now, let's talk about secrets! Everyone knows a little secret sometimes, right? Like a surprise birthday party! But some secrets are very, very important. For countries and armies, some information must be kept super secret. We call this "classified data." It means only a few special people are allowed to know it, to keep everyone safe. This kind of secret information is about how the army works, what special tools they have, or their plans. It's like your teacher keeping the test questions a secret so that everyone tries their best when the test comes.

Who Tells Secrets They Shouldn't?

Sometimes, a person who knows these important secrets might tell them to other people who are not supposed to know. These people are called "leakers." It's like if you found out about a surprise party and told everyone before the party! That would spoil the surprise, wouldn't it? Mr. Trump was very serious about these "leakers." He said that his country was trying to find out who told these secrets. He used a strong phrase, saying they were being "hunted down." This doesn't mean like hunting an animal! It means they were looking very carefully to find out who was sharing information that should have been kept secret. Did you know? Keeping important secrets helps countries stay strong and safe. It's like how a family keeps some things private to help them grow strong together.

Why Are Secrets Important?

Why do countries have secrets? Well, imagine you are playing a game of 'hide and seek.' If you tell everyone where you are hiding, the game isn't fun anymore, and you'll be found very quickly! In a bigger way, armies keep some things secret to be safe and strong. If everyone knows their plans, it makes it harder to protect the country. So, when someone shares a secret that is not supposed to be shared, it can cause problems for the country. That's why Mr. Trump said they were looking for the people who told the secrets.

Making Special Tools

Some of the special tools that armies use are not easy to make. They are called "difficult-to-manufacture weapons." This means they take a long, long time to build. They need very clever engineers and special factories. It's like building a very complicated robot or a huge bridge – it's not something you can just make quickly in your backyard. Some reports, not from Mr. Trump, said that America might have used a lot of these special, hard-to-make tools. But Mr. Trump said that was not true, and they had plenty. Did you know? Some factories in the world are so big, they are like small towns! They employ many people to build amazing things.

What Does This Mean For Us?

For us, here in Africa, this news helps us understand a little bit about how big countries work. It shows us that leaders have to make big decisions about keeping their country safe and about secrets. It also reminds us that information is powerful, and it's important to be careful with secrets. It's like when you share your toys with friends – some toys are for everyone, but some special ones you might want to keep safe for yourself. Countries are a bit like that with their information and tools.

Learning About the World

So, we learned about Mr. Trump, army tools, shortages, and important secrets. The main idea is that Mr. Trump said his country has enough special tools, and he was very serious about finding people who told secrets they shouldn't have. Learning about the news helps us understand the big world around us, and that's a super cool thing! Keep exploring and asking questions, my amazing friends! Until next time, stay curious!
